issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to store the result in a variable named `score_counter` (problem_statement.md lines 21-22). The solution repository, however, declares a variable named `score_cnt` (solution_repository/helloWorld.asm line 4). This name mismatch can confuse students about the required variable name and may cause automated checks or manual grading that expect `score_counter` to fail. The template does not declare any score variable (template_repository/helloWorld.asm has no such declaration), which is acceptable as students likely must add it, but the reference solution's different name remains inconsistent with the specification.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the variable name consistent with the problem statement. Rename the solution's `score_cnt` to `score_counter` (e.g., change `score_cnt dd 0` to `score_counter dd 0`) and, if helpful, add a comment in the template indicating students should declare `score_counter` so expectations are explicit.

issues.description: The problem statement requires students to store the result in a variable named `score_counter`, but the solution repository defines the variable as `score_cnt`. This names the same conceptual entity (the score storage variable) with different identifiers, which will confuse students and likely break any automated checks that expect `score_counter`.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the variable in the solution (and any template/example files if present) to `score_counter` so it matches the explicit requirement in the problem statement (e.g., change `score_cnt dd 0` to `score_counter dd 0`). Alternatively, if `score_cnt` is preferred, update the problem statement to instruct using `score_cnt`—but the names must be aligned to avoid student confusion and grading errors.
